title: Trivial parameters, direct image and fully fixed section formulas
statement:
Work in compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, let $P$ be the profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $P_J$ have profinite continuous left $J$-spaces, continuous equivariant maps and finite jointly surjective covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation on $J$, and $tS=S$ with trivial action [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(P)$ and let $\mathscr E^{\underline J}$ be the category of internal actions: a sheaf $X$ with a natural unital associative action $C(S,J)\times X(S)\to X(S)$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Write $h_T(S)=C(S,T)$, with the induced action when $T\in P_J$. Let $p_J:\mathscr E^{\underline J}\to\mathscr E$ be the geometric morphism whose inverse image is trivial inflation [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], and use $\Phi$ from [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation]. Restriction $\operatorname{res}_t(F)(S)=F(tS)$ is a sheaf on $P$, natural in $F\in\operatorname{Sh}(P_J)$, and there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$p_{J,*}X\simeq\operatorname{res}_t\Phi(X).$$
Its section description identifies $\Phi(X)(tS)$ with
$$X(S)^{\mathrm{all}\ J}=\{x\in X(S):\ \forall f:V\to S,\ \forall g\in C(V,J),\ g\cdot f^*x=f^*x\}.$$
For a commutative condensed ring $R$ with trivial action and $\mathcal R_J=\Phi(R)$, one has $\mathcal R_J(tS)\simeq R(S)$ canonically. For an internal $R$-module $N$ with action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], this gives an $R(S)$-linear identification $\Phi(N)(tS)\simeq N(S)^{\mathrm{all}\ J}$; for any normalized invariants datum $\Gamma_{R,J}$ with its specified inclusion, the latter submodule is identified with $\Gamma_{R,J}(N)(S)$ through that inclusion. The free evaluation $\Phi(N)(H(S))\simeq N(S)$ is linear over $\mathcal R_J(H(S))\simeq R(S)$. For every equivariant linear $v:N\to N'$, the trivial-parameter map is $v_S$ restricted to fully fixed sections and the free-parameter map is the original $v_S$. All these identifications commute with every continuous map of profinite parameters.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-profinite-action-finite-cover-site], $t$ preserves finite limits and covering families. For a finite cover $\{S_i\to S\}$, apply the sheaf equalizer criterion of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] to $F$ and the cover $\{tS_i\to tS\}$. Since $t(S_i\times_S S_j)=tS_i\times_{tS}tS_j$, this is exactly the equalizer criterion for $S\mapsto F(tS)$. Thus restriction is a sheaf, including on the empty cover of the empty parameter. A sheaf map $F\to F\prime$ restricts componentwise at $tS$, and its naturality gives a sheaf map on $P$; identities and compositions are unchanged.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation] to $T=tS$. The action map $\alpha_{tS}$ is the projection $\pi:J\times S\to S$, so identity evaluation identifies $\Phi(X)(tS)$ with the subset of $x\in X(S)$ satisfying $\pi^*x=\gamma\cdot\pi^*x$. Pull this equality back along $(g,f):V\to J\times S$ to obtain $f^*x=g\cdot f^*x$. Conversely the fully fixed condition applied to $V=J\times S$, $f=\pi$, $g=\gamma$ gives that equality. These two implications identify exactly the fully fixed sections, with no test only on ordinary points.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument for returned presentation steps 14,15; no assertion of an external theorem here.

proof.text: Let $A_X=\operatorname{res}_t\Phi(X)$. By step 2 and the restriction and map formulas of [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation], identity evaluation gives a natural sectionwise injective sheaf map $A_X\to X$ whose image consists exactly of fully fixed sections. Its image is stable under restriction: for $x$ fully fixed over $S$, $f:V\to S$, $h:W\to V$ and $g\in C(W,J)$, one has $g\cdot h^*f^*x=(fh)^*x=h^*f^*x$. Give $A_X$ trivial action; the inclusion $i_X:\operatorname{triv}A_X\to X$ is equivariant by the fully fixed condition at the identity parameter map. For a sheaf $Y$ with trivial action, equivariance of $u:Y\to X$ means $g\cdot u_V(z)=u_V(z)$ for every $V,z,g$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Naturality then gives $g\cdot f^*u_S(y)=g\cdot u_V(f^*y)=u_V(f^*y)$, so $u$ factors uniquely through $i_X$. Conversely a factorization through $i_X$ is equivariant. Corestriction and composition with $i_X$ are inverse hom-set maps; both commute with precomposition in $Y$ and postcomposition in $X$. This constructs the adjunction from trivial inflation to $A$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument for returned presentation steps 14,15; no assertion of an external theorem here.

proof.text: The adjunction for $p_J$ in [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction] has the same left adjoint. Here is the canonical comparison explicitly. Its counit $c_X:\operatorname{triv}(p_{J,*}X)\to X$ factors uniquely as the inclusion $i_X:\operatorname{triv}A_X\to X$ after $\operatorname{triv}(a_X)$, defining $a_X:p_{J,*}X\to A_X$. Transpose $i_X$ under the $p_J$ adjunction to define $b_X:A_X\to p_{J,*}X$, so $c_X\operatorname{triv}(b_X)=i_X$. Then $i_X\operatorname{triv}(a_Xb_X)=i_X$ implies $a_Xb_X=1$ by sectionwise injectivity; and $c_X\operatorname{triv}(b_Xa_X)=c_X$ implies $b_Xa_X=1$ by injectivity of the adjunction bijection. Uniqueness of factorization and transposition makes $a$ natural, giving $p_{J,*}\simeq\operatorname{res}_t\Phi$. Explicitly, for an equivariant $v:X\to X\prime$, both $A(v)a_X$ and $a_{X\prime}p_{J,*}(v)$ factor the same map $v c_X$ through $i_{X\prime}$, by naturality of $i$ and $c$. Sectionwise injectivity of $i_{X\prime}$ makes them equal.

proof.text: Give $R$ its trivial action. Step 2 then imposes no condition on $R(S)$, so identity evaluation identifies $\mathcal R_J(tS)$ with $R(S)$, preserving $0,1,+,\cdot$. For $N$ as in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], fully fixed sections form an $R(S)$-submodule: after any $f:V\to S$, $g\cdot(f^*r\,f^*x+f^*y)=f^*r\,(g\cdot f^*x)+g\cdot f^*y=f^*r\,f^*x+f^*y$, and the same calculation applies to negatives and zero. Pointwise operations on equivariant maps $h_{tS}\to N$ evaluate to these operations on $N(S)$, giving the claimed linear identification. By the definition of a normalized invariants datum in that node, its specified inclusion is injective with precisely this image; corestricting that inclusion therefore gives the asserted linear isomorphism with $\Gamma_{R,J}(N)(S)$.

proof.text: For free evaluation use $e_{N,S}$ and its inverse from [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation]. At a parameter $V$ the inverse of $x\in N(S)$ sends $(a,b)$ to $a\cdot b^*x$, and the inverse for $r\in R(S)$ sends $(a,b)$ to $b^*r$, since $R$ has trivial action. Their pointwise product is $(b^*r)(a\cdot b^*x)=a\cdot b^*(rx)$ by the linear action of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Hence inverse evaluation preserves scalar multiplication; the same formula with sums and negatives proves additivity. For $R$ it preserves multiplication and unit as well. Thus $\mathcal R_J(H(S))\simeq R(S)$ is a ring isomorphism and $\Phi(N)(H(S))\simeq N(S)$ is linear over it.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written auxiliary argument for returned presentation steps 14,15; no assertion of an external theorem here.

proof.text: The map formula of [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation] gives $v_S$ restricted to the subset of step 2 on trivial parameters, and $e_{N',S}\Phi(v)_{H(S)}e_{N,S}^{-1}=v_S$ on free parameters. For every continuous $f:V\to S$, trivial evaluation commutes with $f^*$ by the restriction formula in that node. On free parameters, $e_{N,V}\Phi(N)(H(f))=f^*e_{N,S}$ by its parameter naturality (also directly by substituting $(a,f\circ b)$ in step 6). The ring comparisons obey the identical formula with $N=R$. The normalized-invariants comparison commutes with restrictions and module maps because its inclusion is a natural module map and is sectionwise injective [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. This proves all parameter and morphism compatibilities.
